name: Augusto Pinochet
summary: Augusto Pinochet led the military coup that overthrew Salvador Allende, then governed Chile under a dictatorship that repressed political opposition. His government privatized major enterprises, established privately managed individual pension accounts and promulgated a constitution that gave the armed forces a formal role in safeguarding the institutional order.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Pinochet maintained the armed forces, retained army command and gave them a permanent constitutional role.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Law 18,840 empowered the central bank to issue currency and regulate money and credit.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pinochet promulgated Law 18,826, replacing the therapeutic-abortion provision with a prohibition on acts intended to induce abortion.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: Pinochet ratified the Chile–Argentina peace treaty, whose dispute-settlement system commits both states to binding arbitral awards.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pinochet's Decree Law 211 imposed criminal penalties for agreements that limited competition, including agreements on prices, output quotas and market allocation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Pinochet banned Marxist parties by decree and promulgated Article 8, which made organizations promoting violence or totalitarian doctrines unconstitutional.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The transitional provisions left budget legislation with the unelected junta throughout Pinochet's presidential term.

capital-controls.rationale: Under Pinochet's foreign-investment statute, a state committee administered foreign capital entry and investors had to wait three years before repatriating principal.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Decree Law 679 instructed the film classification council to reject films it deemed contrary to morals or good customs.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The constitution established an autonomous central bank, and Law 18,840 gave its own council responsibility for monetary policy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Article 10 granted Chilean nationality to most people born on Chilean soil, even if their parents were foreigners.

class-collaboration.rationale: Pinochet's Chacarillas address urged Chileans across social sectors to unite behind enduring national goals and explicitly rejected class struggle.

class-struggle-history.rationale: At Chacarillas, Pinochet rejected class struggle as a false and divisive account of Chilean society.

conscription.rationale: Pinochet's Decree Law 2306 established compulsory military service and presidential call-ups for service in the army, navy or air force.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Pinochet's junta used an appointed drafting commission and submitted the resulting constitution to a plebiscite, bypassing election of a constituent assembly.

death-penalty.rationale: Pinochet promulgated Law 18,314, which prescribed penalties reaching death for specified terrorism offenses.

democracy-best.rationale: Pinochet overthrew elected president Salvador Allende and kept the presidency under transitional provisions that put military authorities in charge of choosing the sole candidate for the 1988 plebiscite.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The original constitution and its transitional provisions empowered Pinochet to restrict movement and assembly, detain people and order expulsions during emergencies, with limited court review.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Article 19(8) expressly authorized laws restricting the exercise of individual rights or freedoms to protect the environment.

equal-conscription.rationale: The original recruitment decree specifically exempted married women and mothers of minors from military duties.

free-public-college.rationale: The university finance decree provided government-backed loans for annual tuition, including at existing public universities.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pinochet held the presidency and army command simultaneously. Article 32 also vested the president with extensive military powers, including supreme command in war.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: Article 32(5) let the president dissolve the Chamber of Deputies once per term, subject to a ban on dissolution during its last year.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pinochet's Decree Law 2568 set up a process to divide Indigenous reserves into individual holdings under state supervision.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Decree Law 3500 established retirement provision based on individual accounts administered by private pension fund managers in place of the old system for new civilian workers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The economic report documents Pinochet's broad replacement of administered prices with a system in which market prices directed production and distribution.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Article 90 expressly made the armed forces guarantors of the institutional order.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Pinochet's school-finance decree paid private schools to provide publicly subsidized education.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pinochet required schools to offer religious instruction and gave religious authorities responsibility for proposing curricula and certifying teachers.

no-bailouts.rationale: During the banking crisis Pinochet's authorities intervened in major banks and used the central bank to purchase troubled loan portfolios.

no-central-bank.rationale: Pinochet signed the organic law that established the powers and governing council of the Central Bank of Chile.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Decree 924 required schools to offer two hours of religion a week, with attendance optional and religious authorities certifying the teachers.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: In Ego sum Pinochet, he explicitly held that socialism and democracy were incompatible when asked whether a democratic socialist government was possible.

party-controls-media.rationale: The charter's transitional powers enabled Pinochet to restrict publications and broadcasting on security grounds, and the security apparatus used censorship against opposition media.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: As army commander, Pinochet led the September 1973 military coup to remove the elected government and establish a military junta.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Article 19(10) assigned the state responsibility for protecting and expanding Chile's cultural heritage.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Pinochet's stabilization program dismantled much of the price control system and addressed inflation principally through fiscal and monetary restraint.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Pinochet established DINA before the decree legalizing it, and its secret powers enabled detention outside the ordinary judicial process.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 19(24) protected private property, requiring legislation for expropriation, compensation and access to court.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 19(24) expressly subjected property to obligations arising from its social function, including public health, national security and environmental conservation.

proportional-representation.rationale: Pinochet's regime instituted the binomial system, where a list had to double the vote of the next list to take both seats in a district.

public-ownership.rationale: Pinochet's government returned nationalized enterprises to private owners and later privatized major firms, while retaining state ownership of the main copper producer.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pinochet dissolved the previous Congress and replaced the pre-coup constitution with a charter that created a permanent military guardianship and an appointed component of the Senate.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The labor decree confined lawful strikes to regulated bargaining procedures. Article 19(16) barred public employees and workers in certain essential services from striking.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Pinochet led the overthrow of the existing government and then put a new constitutional order in its place.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1980 constitution provided for a Senate alongside the directly elected Chamber of Deputies.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Pinochet signed an amnesty covering offenses during the first years of military rule. A declassified CIA assessment also documents his intervention against extraditing officers implicated in the Letelier case.

separate-church-state.rationale: Under Decree 924, the public school curriculum included religious instruction and religious authorities determined whether instructors were qualified to teach it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pinochet's junta dissolved Congress and displaced the previous constitutional order with a charter that institutionalized military oversight.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Article 92 allowed possession of arms with authorization under the applicable law, while placing those authorizations under government supervision.

state-harmful.rationale: Pinochet promulgated a replacement constitution establishing a Chilean state with a presidency, a legislature and courts.

strong-leader.rationale: Pinochet took the presidency while remaining army commander, and the 1980 charter kept him in office for a further eight years without a competitive presidential election.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Pinochet's junta outlawed Marxist parties, and the intelligence directorate created under his authority targeted opponents for detention and repression.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Pinochet ratified the Convention against Torture with a reservation preserving a military subordinate's superior-orders defense when a superior reiterated an order after the subordinate objected.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Article 19(9) gave the state a duty to guarantee access to health services through either public or private institutions and required equal access to prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Article 25 prohibited immediate presidential reelection under the ordinary constitutional rules, and the transitional provisions specified a separate single extension procedure.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Article 13 set the voting age for Chilean citizens at 18.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1980 constitution gave Chilean citizens over 18 the right to vote and stand for elected office under the same citizenship rules for men and women.

notes: Reviewed every statement, including candidates, against the record. The search covered economic and labor policy, constitutional design and elections, civil liberties and repression, religion and family law, Indigenous land, national culture, international relations, environmental protection, nuclear energy and technology policy, and methods of political change. The UN General Debate and Miller Center indexes yielded no speeches by Pinochet. Read the Chacarillas address, searched the 1981 inaugural address and Ego sum Pinochet, and checked original laws and archival records. The Chile–Argentina treaty provides evidence on arbitration. A research reactor and cabinet discussion of possible power generation do not establish a settled position on building nuclear power plants.
